cards.explanation: The answer is to overcome and conquer. The rider has a bow and a crown, and the text says he "…rode out to overcome and conquer." John sees this right after the Lamb opens the first seal and a living creature calls out "Come!" I'll be honest, friends, I came out of a junk drawer with way less to show for myself than a crown.

The answer is peace. The rider on the bright red horse is granted permission to take away peace from the earth and to make men slay one another. He's also given a great sword. This is a heavy picture, so I'm not going to joke about the horse.

The answer is True. Along with permission to take away peace, the text says the red horse's rider "…was given a great sword." It's the second seal, and the second living creature has just said "Come!" I think this is one of the heavy parts, so I'll just say it plainly.

The answer is prices for wheat and barley. The voice says, "A quart of wheat for a denarius, and three quarts of barley for a denarius, and do not harm the oil and wine." A denarius is a coin. The rider is holding scales, and the voice is counting out what the grain costs.

The answer is Death. The rider on the pale green horse is named Death, and Hades follows close behind. They're given authority over a fourth of the earth. It's a heavy name, so I'll just say it plainly and let it sit.

The answer is False. John says Death is the rider's name, and then adds that Hades followed close behind. They were given authority over a fourth of the earth together. It's a heavy detail, and a careful reading catches it.

The answer is for the word of God and their testimony. John sees the souls of those who had been slain "…for the word of God and for the testimony they had upheld." They're under the altar. I think this is one of the quietest, most serious spots in the whole passage.

The answer is to rest a little while longer. Each of them is given a white robe and told to rest a little while longer. The text says that's until the full number of their fellow servants, their brothers, were killed, just as they had been killed. A white robe and a little rest, and I think that's a kind thing to hand someone.

The answer is that the sun turns black like sackcloth. After the great earthquake, "…the sun became black like sackcloth of goat hair…" The whole moon also turned blood red. Sackcloth of goat hair is rough, dark cloth. I'd say that's a sky nobody's going to forget.

The answer is True. When the Lamb opens the sixth seal, John says "…the whole moon turned blood red…" That comes right alongside the sun going black. Quite a sky, friends, and I should know, since I have one of my own.
The answer is scroll. John says, "The sky receded like a scroll being rolled up…" I think that's the picture he wants us to hold on to. Every mountain and island is moved from its place, too.

The answer is True. John says the sky receded, "…and every mountain and island was moved from its place." Mountains look pretty settled to me, and these moved. I think that tells you how big this moment is.

The answer is caves. John says they "…hid in the caves and among the rocks of the mountains." That's kings, nobles, commanders, the rich, the mighty, and every slave and free man, all hiding in the same spots.

The answer is the One on the throne and the Lamb. The people hiding cry out, "…hide us from the face of the One seated on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb." Notice who is named. It's the One on the throne and the Lamb, not the horses.

The answer is False. The people hiding don't boast. They say, "…the great day of Their wrath has come, and who is able to withstand it?" It's a question they ask while they hide in the caves and rocks.
